title: Horizon Treadmill E1 Speed Sensor Error
shortDescription: Console cannot detect a signal from the speed sensor on the motor.
fullDescription: The E1 error indicates the console is not receiving a speed pulse from the optical or magnetic sensor on the motor flywheel. Without this signal, the controller cannot regulate belt speed and shuts the motor down for safety.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the treadmill at the wall, wait 60 seconds, then power back on.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor cable
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the motor hood and reseat the speed sensor connector at the MCB.

fixSteps.title: Adjust sensor gap
fixSteps.instruction: Set the sensor 3-5 mm from the flywheel magnet and tighten the bracket.

whenToCallPro: Call a technician if reseating the sensor and replacing it does not clear E1 — the motor controller may be defective.
videoSearchQuery: Horizon treadmill E1 error speed sensor fix

faq.q: Can I use the treadmill while E1 shows?
faq.a: No. The motor will not run until the speed signal is restored.

title: Horizon Treadmill E2 Motor Communication Error
shortDescription: Console cannot communicate with the motor control board.
fullDescription: E2 indicates a loss of serial communication between the upper console board and the lower motor control board. Common on Horizon T101/T202 after a firmware glitch or a damaged data cable in the upright tube.

fixSteps.title: Reboot
fixSteps.instruction: Power off for 2 minutes, then back on.

fixSteps.title: Reseat console cable
fixSteps.instruction: Fold the deck up, drop the console, and reseat both ends of the data cable.

whenToCallPro: If reseating cables fails, the lower MCB usually needs replacement by a certified technician.
videoSearchQuery: Horizon E2 error treadmill data cable

faq.a: Yes, MCB and harness are covered under the standard 1-year parts warranty.

title: Horizon Treadmill Running Belt Slipping
shortDescription: Belt hesitates or stalls under foot strike.
fullDescription: When the running belt slips, it usually means tension on the rear roller is too low, or the drive belt between the motor and front roller is worn. Slipping under load causes uneven pace and accelerated belt wear.

fixSteps.title: Tension rear roller
fixSteps.instruction: Turn each rear bolt 1/4 turn clockwise; test; repeat until slipping stops.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate deck
fixSteps.instruction: Apply 100% silicone lubricant under the belt across the deck.

whenToCallPro: Replace drive belt or roller bearings if slipping continues after tension and lube.

faq.q: How tight should the belt be?
faq.a: You should be able to lift each side of the belt 2-3 inches off the deck.

title: Horizon Treadmill Incline Motor Stuck
shortDescription: Deck does not rise or lower when incline buttons are pressed.
fullDescription: The incline motor uses a screw drive to raise the deck. When stuck, the controller logs E5 or simply ignores incline commands. Causes range from a seized screw drive to a failed limit switch.

fixSteps.title: Run incline calibration
fixSteps.instruction: Hold STOP+SPEED-UP for 5 seconds to enter engineering mode and calibrate.

fixSteps.title: Inspect incline motor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove front hood and check that the screw shaft turns freely.

whenToCallPro: If the screw drive is seized, replacement requires removing the deck — call a tech.

faq.a: Calibration fixes about half of cases — mechanical wear needs parts.

title: Horizon Treadmill Console Will Not Power On
shortDescription: Display is blank with the unit plugged into a working outlet.
fullDescription: Horizon treadmills have a circuit breaker on the front of the frame that trips with surges or motor stalls. A tripped breaker, blown fuse, or faulty safety key are the most common causes of a dead console.

fixSteps.title: Reset breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Press the breaker on the front frame in firmly until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Test safety key
fixSteps.instruction: Re-clip the magnetic safety key on the console.

whenToCallPro: Call support if breaker re-trips immediately — this indicates motor or MCB short.
videoSearchQuery: Horizon treadmill no power breaker reset

faq.a: On the front frame next to the power cord inlet.

title: Horizon Treadmill Won't Pair with Phone or Heart Rate Strap
shortDescription: Console does not detect Bluetooth devices in the Horizon Fitness app.
fullDescription: Horizon treadmills broadcast workout data via Bluetooth FTMS to the Horizon Fitness app and to compatible chest straps. Pairing failures usually trace to firmware on the console or a stale pairing cache on the phone.

fixSteps.title: Forget device
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the treadmill from your phone Bluetooth settings, then re-pair via the Horizon app.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Open the Horizon app and accept any console firmware update prompts.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed — only if the console Bluetooth radio is suspected dead after firmware update.

faq.a: Yes via FTMS — pair through the Zwift companion app.

title: Horizon Treadmill Hand-Grip Heart Rate Sensors Not Reading
shortDescription: Pulse display blank when grasping handlebars.
fullDescription: Hand-grip heart rate sensors require dry skin contact and a clean stainless-steel surface. Sweat, hand cream or oxidation prevent the EKG-style sensor from picking up a clean signal.

fixSteps.title: Clean grips
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe stainless grips with isopropyl alcohol; moisten hands slightly.

fixSteps.title: Use chest strap
fixSteps.instruction: Pair an ANT+/Bluetooth strap for accurate readings.

whenToCallPro: Call only if a chest strap also fails to display — points to console pulse receiver fault.
videoSearchQuery: Horizon treadmill heart rate sensor not working

faq.a: They drift during high-intensity intervals — chest straps are far more reliable.

title: Horizon Treadmill Smells Like Burning Rubber or Electronics
shortDescription: Smoke or hot smell from the motor hood during use.
fullDescription: A burning smell on a Horizon treadmill is almost always friction heat between an unlubricated belt and the deck or a failing motor brush. Stop using the unit immediately to avoid fire and motor damage.

fixSteps.title: Stop and unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and unplug immediately; let cool 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate deck
fixSteps.instruction: Apply silicone lubricant under the belt and check tension.

whenToCallPro: If the smell persists after lubrication, the MCB or motor needs professional inspection.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep using?
faq.a: No — running with friction heat can melt the belt and short the motor.

title: Horizon Treadmill Belt Drifts Left or Right
shortDescription: Belt walks toward one side of the deck.
fullDescription: Belt drift means the rear roller is not perpendicular to the deck. Adjusting the rear bolts incrementally re-centers the belt. Running with a drifted belt frays edges and damages the deck.

fixSteps.title: Level the unit
fixSteps.instruction: Adjust the rear levelers so the treadmill sits flat.

fixSteps.title: Adjust drift
fixSteps.instruction: If belt drifts right, turn right rear bolt 1/4 clockwise; if left, turn left bolt.

whenToCallPro: Call only if the belt edge is shredded — replacement needed.

title: Horizon Fitness App Not Syncing Workouts
shortDescription: Completed workouts do not appear in app history.
fullDescription: The Horizon Fitness app uploads workout data after the session ends if the phone stays in Bluetooth range. Sync failures are usually caused by leaving Bluetooth range early or app permissions being revoked.

fixSteps.title: Stay paired
fixSteps.instruction: Keep the phone near the console until the workout summary uploads.

fixSteps.title: Permissions
fixSteps.instruction: Grant Bluetooth and Background App Refresh permissions to the Horizon Fitness app.

faq.q: Can I sync to Apple Health?
faq.a: Yes — enable the Apple Health toggle in app settings.
